headline: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics and PET-CT & SPECT-CT facilities at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics and PET-CT & SPECT-CT facilities at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital

Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics integrates Video Urodynamics (VUDS) with Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) -based brain mapping; first such approach being attempted in India

New diagnostic facilities to benefit approximately 5,600 patients annually at affordable cost

03 SEP 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, today inaugurated the Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics in the Department of Urology and the PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities in the Department of Nuclear Medicine at VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi.

During his visit, Shri J.P. Nadda also visited the Heart Command Centre and the Sports Injury Centre at Safdarjung Hospital and reviewed the services and activities being undertaken at these centres.

During the detailed review of the functioning and ongoing projects of Safdarjung Hospital, Shri J.P. Nadda emphasised the need for regular review of projects and periodic inspection of projects in the pipeline. He stressed the importance of setting practical and achievable timelines for completion of projects to ensure their timely implementation. The Union Health Minister also appreciated the distinct identity and reputation that Safdarjung Hospital has established over the years and noted that the institution has developed its own unique name and standing in the healthcare sector.

Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics

The Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics has been established with Video Urodynamics (VUDS) integrated with Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS). The facility will enable detailed assessment of bladder function and support diagnosis of urinary bladder disorders, including complex cases associated with neurological conditions.

An important feature of the Centre is the integration of VUDS with brain mapping through NIRS, an approach being attempted for the first time in India. It enables assessment of changes in cerebral blood oxygenation during bladder filling and emptying and may assist clinicians in determining whether a bladder disorder is of bladder-related, neurological or combined origin.

The Centre is expected to cater to approximately 5,000 patients annually, thereby strengthening the availability of specialised urological diagnostic services at the hospital.

PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities

The newly installed PET-CT and SPECT-CT facilities in the Department of Nuclear Medicine will augment the hospital’s diagnostic capabilities in several specialised areas, including cancer care, cardiology, neurology, renal diseases and endocrinology.

The PET-CT facility will support cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment planning and follow-up, besides facilitating advanced imaging required for specialised therapies. It will further support multidisciplinary clinical management involving Medical Oncology, Radiation Oncology, Hematology, Urology, Nephrology and Pediatric Oncology.

The SPECT-CT facility will strengthen diagnostic services for cardiac, renal, endocrine, orthopaedic and gastrointestinal conditions, thereby facilitating comprehensive diagnostic evaluation and appropriate clinical management. The advanced Nuclear Medicine services are expected to benefit approximately 600–700 patients annually and will be made available at an affordable cost.

The addition of these services marks a further strengthening of the specialised healthcare infrastructure at VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital. The Centre for Advanced Bladder Diagnostics, PET-CT and SPECT-CT services will facilitate comprehensive diagnostic evaluation, support timely treatment planning and further strengthen multidisciplinary patient care.

headline: NFDC-NFAI and FTII to Organise Specialised Workshop on Moving Image Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration
fullText:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting

NFDC-NFAI and FTII to Organise Specialised Workshop on Moving Image Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration

03 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai/Pune, 3 September 2026

The NFDC-National Film Archive of India (NFDC-NFAI), in association with the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, will organise a specialised workshop on “Moving Images: Preservation, Archiving, Digitization and Restoration” from October 5 to 15, 2026, excluding weekends, at the NFDC-NFAI and FTII campuses in Pune.

The workshop is designed for students, aspiring professionals, researchers and others interested in film preservation, archiving, restoration, film technology and audiovisual heritage. It will provide participants with an understanding of the art, science and practice of preserving moving images through classroom sessions, practical demonstrations, hands-on training, institutional visits and screenings of archival and restored films.

The programme will cover important areas including moving image preservation, metadata, digital preservation, film types and bases, preventive conservation, digital film restoration, paper conservation and audio restoration. Practical sessions will include film identification, inspection and repair, manual film cleaning, celluloid and digital film projection, film scanning and digitization. Participants will also learn about film scanners, picture and audio scanning, storage requirements, colour grading and quality control.

Participants will get first-hand exposure to the working environment and facilities of NFDC-NFAI, including its Library and Vaults, Documentation and Projection Room. The workshop will also provide exposure to professional restoration workflows with support from Prasad Corp., which will contribute its technical expertise and equipment for film repair, conservation and digital restoration.

The programme will include institutional visits to NFDC-National Film Archive of India, FTII, Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and Reserve Bank of India Archives. These visits will familiarise participants with different approaches to preservation, documentation, conservation and management of archival collections.

An international perspective will be provided through a dedicated session on practices followed by the Thai Film Archive. Archival and restored film screenings, including presentations on 35mm and digital formats, will also form an important part of the programme.

Speaking on the initiative, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Vice-Chancellor, FTII, said the programme brings together film education and preservation of cinematic heritage and will provide participants with academic learning, practical exposure and access to specialised facilities.

Shri Prakash Magdum, Managing Director, NFDC, said the initiative aims to share institutional experience and specialised skills with students and aspiring professionals and encourage greater interest in film preservation.

Shri Abhishek Prasad, Director & CTO, Prasad Corp., said the collaboration will help nurture the next generation of preservation professionals by sharing industry experience and technology.

The course will be led by Aparna Subramanian, Course Director, with a maximum intake of 24 participants. The course fee is ₹12,000 per participant.

headline: EPFO urges eligible establishments to settle long-pending EPF damages disputes at substantially reduced rates under VISHWAS, 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

EPFO urges eligible establishments to settle long-pending EPF damages disputes at substantially reduced rates under VISHWAS, 2026

High Courts endorse the Scheme, encourage establishments to avail benefits

03 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has launched VISHWAS, 2026, a one-time settlement scheme that allows employers to close long-pending disputes by paying a sharply reduced penalty amount.The Scheme will remain open until 28 December 2026. Employers are encouraged to apply within this period, as the closing date will not be extended.

Under normal rules, the penalty for late PF deposit can be as high as 37% per year. Under VISHWAS, 2026, the penalty has been reduced as follows:

Delay for up to 2 months: pay only 0.25% per month,

Delay from 2 to 4 months: pay only 0.50% per month,

Delay beyond 4 months: pay only 1% per month.

The Hon'ble Bombay High Court (Pune Bench), in WP No. 4246 of 2018, ordered an employer to apply under VISHWAS, 2026 within two weeks, modified the earlier tribunal order accordingly, and disposed of the writ petition. The Hon'ble Madras High Court disposed of WP No. 38008 of 2024 the moment the employer expressed willingness to avail the Scheme, closing the writ petition and related tribunal proceedings simultaneously. The Hon'ble Kerala High Court (Ernakulam Bench) has gone a step further and issued similar directions in nineteen separate cases, directing those establishments to approach EPFO and settle under VISHWAS, 2026.

In a significant relief measure for employers, cases relating to delayed payment of Provident Fund (PF) contributions prior to 14 June 2024 may be considered under the applicable provisions, provided the employer falls within specified categories. The coverage includes cases where proceedings relating to penalties are currently pending before a court or tribunal; cases where the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has already passed a penalty order but recovery, either fully or partially, is still pending; cases where EPFO has issued a notice proposing the imposition of a penalty but a final order has not yet been passed; and cases where EPFO records reflect delays in PF payments but no penalty notice has been issued so far.

The entire process has been made available through an online mechanism. Employers are required to first clear all outstanding interest on delayed PF contributions before submitting an application. Thereafter, they may log on to the EPFO Employer Portal at https://unifiedportal-emp.epfindia.gov.in, access the VISHWAS, 2026 module, select the applicable category, upload the required documents and complete the process through digital authentication.

The system will automatically calculate the revised penalty amount. Employers will be provided 15 days to make the payment, with an automatic extension of a further 15 days, wherever required. Upon confirmation of payment, EPFO will issue a digitally signed Settlement Certificate, following which the concerned proceedings pending before a court or tribunal shall stand closed.

Employers are encouraged to avail the benefits of the Scheme before its closure on 28 December 2026. Assistance is available at all 153 EPFO Regional Offices across the country, where dedicated VISHWAS Cells and Helpdesks have been established to facilitate and assist applicants. Detailed guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions are available on the EPFO website. For further assistance, employers may also contact the toll-free helpline at 1800-180-1820.

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Occupational Safety Training under NAMASTE Scheme Inaugurated in West Bengal: First Batch Begins for Sanitation Workers of Durgapur Municipal Corporation

Five Day Programme to Promote Safe Practices and Mechanised Sanitation; West Bengal Profiles 7,630 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers

We need to provide sanitation workers with a safe, dignified and mechanised working environment: Smt. Agnimitra Paul

03 SEP 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Occupational Safety Training Programme under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme was inaugurated in West Bengal, with the first batch commencing for sanitation workers of the Durgapur Municipal Corporation.

The programme was organised under the NAMASTE Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, with technical support from the CSIR-Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-CMERI).

The programme was inaugurated in the presence of Smt. Agnimitra Paul, Minister-in-Charge, Urban Development and Municipal Affairs, Government of West Bengal.

Senior officials and representatives from CSIR-CMERI, the State Urban Development Agency, Asansol Municipal Corporation, Durgapur Municipal Corporation and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) also attended the programme.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Agnimitra Paul highlighted the importance of providing sanitation workers with a safe, dignified and mechanised working environment. She reiterated the commitment to eliminating hazardous cleaning practices through training, appropriate safety equipment and increased adoption of mechanised sanitation solutions.

Smt. Agnimitra Paul appreciated the support extended by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, NSKFDC and CSIR-CMERI in strengthening the safety and capacity of sanitation workers in West Bengal. She emphasised that sanitation workers perform an essential role in keeping cities clean and healthy, and that safeguarding their dignity, safety and well-being is a collective responsibility.

West Bengal has completed the profiling of 7,630 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers. Personal Protective Equipment kits have also been distributed among identified workers. Awareness workshops on preventing hazardous sanitation practices have been conducted across 124 municipalities and three cantonment boards in the State.

To strengthen emergency preparedness, the blood-group details of sanitation workers have been collected and an emergency database has been created to facilitate timely assistance during critical situations.

Identity Cards were also distributed to sanitation workers during the programme. The initiative recognises sanitation workers as an integral part of the urban sanitation ecosystem and reinforces the dignity and importance of their work.

Safaimitras from the Durgapur Municipal Corporation participated in the programme. An audio-visual safety walk demonstrating the importance and correct use of Personal Protective Equipment was presented. The dignitaries also visited the Swachh Bharat Test Bed and the training facility for Safaimitras developed by CSIR-CMERI.

The Occupational Safety Training programme will be conducted over five days and comprise 30 hours of instruction. Each batch will accommodate a maximum of 45 sanitation workers.

An assessment will be conducted after completion of the training. Participants maintaining at least 70 per cent attendance will receive a certificate and a stipend of Rs 1,000.

The training will enhance the knowledge and practical skills of sanitation workers in occupational safety, appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment, safe working practices, emergency response and mechanised sanitation operations.

In the first phase, the training programme is being implemented in Durgapur Municipal Corporation, Asansol Municipal Corporation, Bardhaman Municipality, Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation and Chandannagar Municipal Corporation. It will subsequently be expanded to other municipalities in the State in a phased manner.

As part of the initiative, CSIR-CMERI is proposed to serve as a one-stop institutional centre for sanitation-worker safety and mechanisation. It will provide an integrated platform for occupational safety training, testing and assessment of safety equipment, and verification of equipment and devices used in sanitation operations.

The institutional mechanism will promote the adoption of appropriate and reliable safety equipment by facilitating systematic testing against relevant technical and safety requirements. It will also support the capacity-building of sanitation workers and other stakeholders through structured technical and practical training.

By bringing together training, technology, testing and equipment verification under one institutional framework, the initiative will help Urban Local Bodies make informed decisions concerning safety equipment and mechanised sanitation solutions.

The NAMASTE Scheme promotes the safety, dignity and socio-economic well-being of sanitation workers while supporting the mechanisation of sanitation work and elimination of hazardous cleaning practices.

The Scheme seeks to ensure that sanitation workers are not required to undertake hazardous manual entry into sewers or septic tanks. Urban Local Bodies, government and private organisations, contractors and other agencies engaged in sanitation operations are expected to follow prescribed safety procedures and adopt mechanised solutions.

The programme reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of India and the Government of West Bengal to building a safer, mechanised and dignified sanitation ecosystem.

Safety, dignity and mechanisation remain the three foundational pillars of the NAMASTE Scheme.

headline: India and Belgium call for deeper defence industrial collaboration to build stronger militaries through co-development & co-production

India and Belgium call for deeper defence industrial collaboration to build stronger militaries through co-development & co-production

03 SEP 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of Defence & Foreign Trade of Belgium Mr Theo Francken has emphasised the strong potential for deeper industrial collaboration between India and Belgium to strengthen the defence forces through collective efforts, with Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth urging Belgian defence manufacturers to leverage their technological expertise alongside India’s manufacturing scale for co-development & co-production of niche products for shared security and prosperity. The two Ministers graced the India-Belgium Defence CEOs Roundtable and B2B Meetings in New Delhi on September 03, 2026. The event was attended by the representatives of the Belgian industry, Confederation of Indian Industry and Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers.

The Belgium Defence Minister underscored the growing strategic partnership between India and the European Union (EU), highlighting the robust dialogue structures developing across maritime security, information security and aerospace. He stated that these institutional frameworks have established India as a trusted partner for the EU.

Commending the dynamism of Indian entrepreneurs, Mr Theo Francken stressed the need to bolster the two militaries in the evolving security environment through joint efforts. “United we stand, divided we fall,” he said.

Highlighting the strategic transformation of India’s defence manufacturing sector, Raksha Rajya Mantri stated that the nation is decisively moving from import dependence to indigenous capability, trusted partnerships, and global competitiveness through initiatives such as Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make-in-India. “This transformation is outward-facing. Strategic autonomy is best secured through credible, mutually beneficial international collaboration,” he said.

Shri Sanjay Seth emphasised that India and Belgium can leverage their strengths and prioritise collaboration in areas including cyber security, AI-enabled unmanned aerial systems, underwater domain vehicles, and complex weapon systems. He stated that innovation platforms like iDEX and ADITI are engaging start-ups and MSMEs in AI, quantum technologies, military communications, anti-drone systems, and adaptive camouflage, providing “excellent avenues for bilateral R&D and industrialisation”.

Raksha Rajya Mantri pointed out that India’s defence industrial base today combines Defence Public Sector Units, a growing private sector, and over 16,000 MSMEs, with domestic industry delivering advanced capabilities across aerospace, naval and land platforms, defence electronics, cyber security, space technologies, and unmanned systems. Through Department of Defence Production-led measures, India is accelerating capacity building, strengthening value chains, and incentivising technology transfer and co-development, he said.

Shri Sanjay Seth underlined that India has liberalised Foreign Direct Investment in defence up to 74% under the automatic route and up to 100% through the government route to enable partnerships in niche technologies. “The new space policy permits 100% FDI. Dedicated Defence Industrial Corridors in Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, with further corridors planned in Maharashtra, Assam and other regions, offer competitive incentives and ecosystem support for foreign original equipment manufacturers and partners,” he added.

During the event, multiple MoUs were exchanged towards leveraging Belgian technology with Indian skill and scale.
